definitions.average_baseline: Today's balance plus 14 x the average daily net cash flow of the 63-day history (the 'historical average' forecast; ignores recorded bills and invoices).
definitions.balance_error: Absolute difference between forecast and realised balance on day 14 (rupees); the naive baseline forecast is today's balance minus recorded bills, ignoring sales and collections.
definitions.band_coverage: Share of businesses whose realised day-14 balance fell inside the forecast band. The band is sized as an 80% range for everyday sales/expense noise only; it does not model late customer payments, so coverage is reported separately for businesses with and without open invoices.
definitions.false_positive_rate: No-shortage businesses wrongly warned / all no-shortage businesses.
definitions.labelled_shortage: The realised (hidden) balance drops below Rs. 0 on any day 1-14.
definitions.lead_time: For correctly warned businesses: days from the forecast date to the first realised negative day (how much notice the owner gets).
definitions.naive_rule: Warn if today's balance minus recorded bills due within 14 days is below zero.
definitions.precision: Predicted shortages that really happened / all predicted shortages.
definitions.predicted_shortage: The forecast's projected balance drops below Rs. 0 on any day 1-14.
definitions.recall: Labelled shortages that were predicted / all labelled shortages.
definitions.split: Time-based: each synthetic business has 63 days of history the model may see, then a hidden 14-day future generated afterwards with fresh noise and customer lateness. Labels come only from that hidden future, so no future information leaks into the forecast.

limitations: Synthetic data follows our own assumptions about small-shop cash flows, so these figures show how the software behaves, not how it performs for real businesses. Real-world validation is still needed.
method: Synthetic micro-businesses (fixed seed). The forecaster sees 9 weeks of history plus recorded bills and invoices; labels come from a hidden 14-day future generated with fresh noise and customer lateness. The naive baseline subtracts recorded bills from today's cash and ignores sales and collections.
